title: Post from @MarisolBakesOH: "Charged TWICE"

fields.avatarBrief: smiling woman in her thirties in a flour-dusted apron in a home kitchen, holding a tray of cupcakes, casual phone selfie
fields.text: @TallisHome you charged my card TWICE for the Clean Sweep mop pad subscription AGAIN this month. $18.99 x2. Is this the hack?? Nobody answers the care line. #TallisFail #TallisHack
fields.attachedImageBrief: phone photo of a smartphone held over a kitchen counter, showing a banking app transaction list with two identical lines circled in red marker-style drawing, a box of mop refill pads blurred in the background
fields.attachedImageAlt: Banking app screen with two identical charges circled

instructorNote: This is a noise inject. The double charge comes from a known defect in the March 1 subscription renewal run, which Customer Care logged on March 3. It has nothing to do with the export. Watch whether SOCIAL records the post word for word with the time and the account under the rumor protocol, passes it to Customer Care as a billing defect, stays silent in public until COMMS approves a reply, and keeps it out of the breach narrative on the 10:00 listening report.

citations.headingPath: TMPCDI › 5. Rumor and false claim protocol
citations.quote: 1. Social listening flags a claim that appears on three or more accounts, or on one account with more than 5,000 followers, or in a reporter's question. 2. Social Media Manager records the claim word

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Candid phone snapshot taken in a bright home kitchen in the morning. A woman's hand holds a smartphone flat over a speckled granite kitchen counter, the screen glowing white with a banking app list of rows too small to read from this distance. Two neighbouring rows are loosely circled by hand in thick red digital marker strokes. In the soft-focus background, a plain unbranded cardboard box of mop refill pads sits next to a coffee mug and a flour-dusted mixing bowl. Window light comes from the left, with a slight downward tilt, shallow depth of field and a casual, slightly irritated mood. Setting: outside a building entrance: a small crowd of reporters and a TV camera on a tripod, a van with a mast folded down, a plain sidewalk, overcast sky
